text: Anthropic's list API price for Claude Sonnet 5.5 is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Cross-checked on claude.com/pricing (HS8, same owner, so not independent).

text: Anthropic's list API price for Claude Opus 5.5 is $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Also shown on claude.com/pricing (same owner).

text: Claude Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens, and $0.50/$2.50 for prompts over 100,000 tokens.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Long-context C-file prompts would usually exceed 100K tokens, so the higher tier applies.

text: Anthropic's top tier (Claude Fable 5.1) is listed at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often.

text: Anthropic's Opus-tier list price fell from $5/$25 (Opus 4.5 through Opus 5) to $4/$20 per million tokens (Opus 5.5).
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Trend observation from one price table. It does not guarantee future cuts.

text: Anthropic made Claude Sonnet 5's introductory $2/$10 per-million-token price its standard price, cancelling a scheduled increase to $3/$15.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Shows that LLM input costs can move in either direction on short notice. Build pricing headroom into the model.

text: Claude models from 4.7 onward use a tokenizer that produces about 30% more tokens for the same text than earlier models.
notes: Cost-per-page estimates built on older token ratios understate the cost on new models by about 30%.

text: Anthropic's Batch API gives a 50% discount on both input and output tokens (e.g., Sonnet 5.5 batch is $1/$5 per million).
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Suits done-for-you per-file reviews, which can tolerate asynchronous turnaround.

text: Anthropic batches return results within 24 hours at most (most finish in under 1 hour), and results stay retrievable for 29 days.
notes: Batches that do not finish within 24 hours expire, and the doc warns that more requests may expire under high demand.

text: A single Anthropic Message Batch is capped at 100,000 requests or 256 MB, whichever comes first.
notes: Not a constraint at solo-operator volumes.

text: On Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, prompt-cache reads cost 0.05x the base input price, while cache writes cost 1.25x (5-minute) or 2x (1-hour).
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Running repeated CUE/effective-date passes over the same cached C-file prefix would cost about 5% of base input after the first write.

text: Anthropic's batch, prompt-caching and data-residency pricing modifiers stack multiplicatively.
notes: So a batched, cached read on Sonnet 5.5 is about $0.05/MTok (0.05x of the $1 batch rate). That figure is arithmetic, not a quoted number.

text: Claude 4.6-and-later models (except Haiku 5.5) offer a 1M-token context window at the standard per-token price, with no long-context surcharge.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often.

text: Requesting US-only inference on Claude 4.6+ models adds a 1.1x multiplier to all token prices.
notes: Relevant if law-firm buyers require US-only data processing for veteran PII/PHI.

text: When Claude ingests a PDF natively, each page typically costs 1,500-3,000 text tokens, plus image tokens because each page is also converted to an image, with no separate PDF fee.
notes: Native PDF ingestion is roughly twice a text-only read, because every page carries both text and image tokens.

text: Claude 4.7-and-later models process images at a high-resolution tier of up to 4,784 visual tokens per image, roughly three times the standard tier.
notes: Downsampling page images before sending them limits cost. Visual tokens = ceil(w/28) x ceil(h/28).

text: A single Claude request accepts at most 600 PDF pages (100 when the context window is under 1M tokens), and dense PDFs can fill the context window sooner.
notes: A multi-thousand-page C-file would have to be split across several requests (chunking, map-reduce). That design choice affects both cost and accuracy.

text: DERIVED ESTIMATE: one native-PDF pass over 1,000 C-file pages on Claude Sonnet 5.5 costs about $6-$16 in input tokens at list price, or about $3-$8 via Batch.
notes: Arithmetic, not a quoted figure. Assumes 1,500-3,000 text tokens plus about 1,300-4,800 image tokens per page (2.8-7.8M tokens per 1,000 pages) at $2/MTok. Output tokens, retries and multiple passes are excluded. C-file page counts are UNSOURCED (gap), so per-file cost scales with an unverified page count.

text: Google Cloud Vision Document Text Detection (OCR) is free for the first 1,000 units per month, then $1.50 per 1,000 units up to 5M units per month, and $0.60 per 1,000 above that.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. The table was extracted with flattened cells, and the fetch tool inferred the column mapping. Third-party leads for Textract, Document AI and Azure DI give the same $1.50/$0.60 structure (HS11-HS13, unreachable, not evidence).

text: Google Cloud Vision bills each page of a multi-page PDF as an individual image (one billable unit per feature per page).
notes: So OCR of a 1,000-page file costs about $1.50 at the standard tier.

text: DERIVED ESTIMATE: an OCR-first pipeline (Vision OCR, then a text-only read on Sonnet 5.5) costs about $4.50-$7.50 per 1,000 pages for the first pass, and later cached passes cost about $0.15-$0.30 in input tokens per 1,000 pages.
notes: Arithmetic, not a quoted figure. Assumes Anthropic's 1,500-3,000 tokens per page also applies to OCR text, and ignores the +30% tokenizer effect (HC7), output tokens and cache-write cost. The two owners are Google and Anthropic. Its main use is showing that inference is a small cost per file compared with likely per-file prices.

text: By default, Anthropic does not retain API prompts and outputs; the exception is 'Covered Models', which require 30-day retention.
notes: CONFLICT RISK: earlier, widely cited Anthropic policy was 30-day API retention, but that policy page (privacy.claude.com) was unreachable, so the conflict could not be checked. Confirm against the commercial data retention policy before telling law-firm buyers.

text: Anthropic states it does not use retained API data (or uploaded images) for model training without the customer's express permission.
notes: Useful answer to law-firm vendor-security questionnaires about subprocessors. It does not replace the vendor's own controls.

text: Zero Data Retention on the Claude API is enabled per organization through Anthropic sales, not self-serve.
notes: A solo founder may face sales-qualification friction getting ZDR.

text: Anthropic's top-tier Covered Models (Fable 5/5.1, Mythos 5/5.1) require 30-day data retention, so they cannot be used under ZDR without Anthropic's express authorization.
notes: A vendor that promises law firms zero retention would be limited to Opus/Sonnet/Haiku-tier models.

text: Eligible organizations can sign Anthropic's standard BAA and enable HIPAA readiness self-serve from the Claude Console.
notes: C-files contain medical records (PHI-like data). VA claims work is not automatically HIPAA-covered, but buyers may ask for HIPAA-grade handling. Beta features and some tools are excluded from the BAA.

text: Anthropic Files API operations (upload, list, delete) are free; file content is billed only as input tokens when used, with limits of 500 MB per file and 1 TB per organization.
notes: Storage of C-files on the LLM vendor side has no direct fee.

text: The Anthropic Files API is not eligible for Zero Data Retention.
notes: Inferred from a page-metadata flag. An architecture promising ZDR would need to send documents inline rather than via file_id.

text: Anthropic recommends one workspace per tenant for multi-tenant Files API isolation, and an organization gets up to 100 workspaces by default.
notes: Per-firm data isolation past about 100 firm customers would need the Anthropic account team. Workspace IDs are also shared across all keys with workspace access.

text: With Claude's citations feature, the returned cited_text does not count toward output tokens, though enabling citations slightly increases input tokens.
notes: Lowers the cost of citation-grounded draft instruments. The gain is largest when quoting from documents.

text: Claude Enterprise is listed at US$20 per seat per month billed annually with a 20-seat minimum, with usage billed separately at API rates.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Extracted by the WebFetch summarizer. The usage clause (HE46) is the summarizer's wording, not a verbatim quote. This is a low general-purpose AI seat anchor that firm buyers may compare a vertical tool against.

text: Claude Team plan seats are listed at $20/month (annual) or $25 (monthly) for Standard, and $100 (annual) or $125 (monthly) for Premium.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. Extracted by the WebFetch summarizer. The headline numbers $20 and $100 come from the summary, and the quoted strings carry the monthly-billing figures.

text: Anthropic's Claude Startups program offers up to $100K in additional API credits only through partner VCs, so a bootstrapped founder can access at most partner discounts worth up to $45,000.
notes: Price as shown on 2026-10-19; vendor prices change often. The 'only through VCs' reading comes from 'claimed through your VC'. Credits are limited to the first-party API.

text: As of 2026-10-19, Anthropic's Claude Startups program was not accepting new applications.
notes: Time-sensitive. A bootstrapped founder should not budget for startup credits.

text: Anthropic says API volume discounts may be negotiated case by case for high-volume users.
notes: Not likely to matter at solo-operator volumes.
